alternatives_and_negative_results: Do not add general peak tolerance, suppress the difference or claim Float/Fixed peak equality.
applicability: RTL peak selection and target-list grouping for quantized power maps.
assessed_root_cause: Quantization breaks the Float exact equality before grouping; the integer grouping implementation follows its own approved stored-power ordering.
author_role: historical project engineering record, backfilled by FPGA engineering copilot
chosen_corrective_method: Preserve both exact powers and classify only the narrowly defined historical exception; keep the Fixed integer peak rule and require same unchanged component plus exact independent records.
generalizable_lesson: When quantization changes a tie, localize the difference to the stage where ordering changes and validate the downstream algorithm against its own frozen contract.
initial_faulty_assumption_or_design_deci: Any Float/Fixed peak-coordinate difference could be treated as a grouping bug or waived with a broad coordinate tolerance.
non_applicability: Does not permit new peak-coordinate mismatches or waive new two-target separation requirements.
observable_consequence: Float chooses (3,20) by its tie rule; fixed integer powers select (4,20) by the frozen maximum stored-power rule. CFAR masks and 107-cell component membership are identical, and independent integer grouping/records match.
observed_problem: Two historical phase-interference vectors have an exact Float power tie at adjacent range cells, while quantized stored integer powers differ.
repeatable_validation: Replay the two historical vectors, check exact Float tie, Fixed power difference, identical masks/component cells and independent union-find records.
reviewer_role: documentary evidence validation by FPGA engineering copilot; not a separate human reviewer
safety_contract_constraints: Keep the exception limited to the two named historical vectors and approved C06 D conditions.
title: Distinguish quantization-induced peak tie splitting from a grouping implementation defect
